_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Bantu Origins and Early Peoples of Cameroon
910.label: Event
910.description: The Cameroon-Nigeria borderland is the probable Bantu homeland; early ironworking and agricultural communities spread across the region.

910.name: Bantu Cradle and Proto-Bantu Dispersal
910.label: Event
910.description: Linguistic and archaeological evidence places the proto-Bantu homeland in the Cameroon Grassfields; initial southward and eastward migrations begin.

910.name: Early Ironworking and Settlement
910.label: Event
910.description: Iron smelting develops in the Mandara Mountains and Grassfields; yam and oil-palm cultivation supports population growth.

910.name: Sao Civilisation of the Lake Chad Basin
910.label: Event
910.description: The Sao people build fortified settlements in the Logone-Chari floodplain; terracotta figurines and bronze-working flourish.

910.name: Sao Walled Settlements
910.label: Event
910.description: Sao mound settlements along the Logone and Chari rivers; distinctive terracotta sculpture tradition; fishing and agriculture.

910.name: Sao Decline and Kotoko Succession
910.label: Event
910.description: Kanem-Bornu expansion absorbs Sao communities; Kotoko city-states emerge as successors in the far north.

920.name: Kanem-Bornu Influence in Northern Cameroon
920.label: Event
920.description: The Kanem-Bornu Empire extends suzerainty over Mandara, Kotoko, and other northern Cameroon polities; Islam spreads via trade and conquest.

920.name: Mandara Sultanate
920.label: Event
920.description: Mandara kingdom in the Mandara Mountains converts to Islam; mediates between Bornu and southern highland peoples.

920.name: Trans-Saharan and Trans-Sudanic Trade
920.label: Event
920.description: Slave, ivory, and cloth trade links northern Cameroon to Bornu, Tripoli, and the Hausa states.

920.name: Grassfields Kingdoms and Bamoun Sultanate
920.label: Event
920.description: Tikar-related chiefdoms and the Bamoun Sultanate develop centralised kingdoms in the western highlands; artistic traditions flourish.

920.name: Bamoun Sultanate and King Njoya
920.label: Event
920.description: The Bamoun Sultanate under Sultan Njoya develops a unique script (Shu Mom), converts to Islam, and creates an elaborate court culture.

920.name: Bamileke and Tikar Chiefdoms
920.label: Event
920.description: Decentralised but hierarchical Bamileke chiefdoms in the western highlands; elaborate secret societies and masquerade traditions.

930.name: Fulani Jihad and Adamawa Emirate
930.label: Event
930.description: Modibbo Adama leads Fulani jihad into northern Cameroon as part of the Sokoto Caliphate; Adamawa Emirate transforms the region.

930.name: Founding of the Adamawa Emirate
930.label: Event
930.description: Modibbo Adama receives a flag from Usman dan Fodio; establishes Yola as capital; subordinate lamidates across northern Cameroon.

930.name: Fulani Slave Raiding and Resistance
930.label: Event
930.description: Fulani lamidates raid non-Muslim 'kirdi' peoples of the Mandara Mountains and Adamawa Plateau; fierce resistance from Gbaya and other groups.

940.name: German Kamerun (1884–1916)
940.label: Event
940.description: Germany establishes Kamerun protectorate; plantation economy on the coast; expansion into interior; World War I campaigns end German rule.

940.name: German Annexation and Gustav Nachtigal
940.label: Event
940.description: Gustav Nachtigal signs treaties with Douala chiefs; Kamerun protectorate proclaimed at Scramble for Africa; coastal plantation economy (cocoa, rubber, palm oil).

940.name: German Conquest of the Interior
940.label: Event
940.description: Military expeditions subdue Adamawa, Bamoun, and Bamileke areas; forced labour for railways and plantations; Neukamerun acquired from France 1911.

940.name: French and British Mandates (1916–1960)
940.label: Event
940.description: League of Nations mandates divide Cameroon; French Cameroun (80%) and British Cameroons develop under different colonial systems.

940.name: French Cameroun Mandate and Trusteeship
940.label: Event
940.description: Indigénat system; forced labour for infrastructure; UPC nationalist movement; brutal suppression of Bamileke insurrection (1955–1960).

940.name: British Cameroons and the Plebiscite
940.label: Event
940.description: British Cameroons administered as part of Nigeria; 1961 plebiscite: Northern Cameroons joins Nigeria, Southern Cameroons joins Cameroun Republic.

950.name: Ahmadou Ahidjo and Nation-Building
950.label: Event
950.description: Ahidjo leads independent Cameroon; federal then unitary state; one-party CNU rule; suppression of UPC insurgency; oil economy begins.

950.name: Independence and Reunification
950.label: Event
950.description: French Cameroun independent 1 January 1960; Southern Cameroons reunification creates Federal Republic 1 October 1961.

950.name: Ahidjo's Unitary One-Party State
950.label: Event
950.description: Federation abolished 1972 (United Republic); single-party CNU regime; political centralisation; Ahidjo resigns 1982, hands power to Biya.

960.name: Paul Biya Era (1982–Present)
960.label: Event
960.description: Biya becomes one of Africa's longest-ruling leaders; multiparty transition; economic crisis; Anglophone crisis escalates to armed conflict; Boko Haram spillover in the Far North.

960.name: Biya's Consolidation of Power
960.label: Event
960.description: Failed 1984 coup; Ahidjo exiled; CPDM replaces CNU; austerity under structural adjustment; democratic opening under pressure.

960.name: Multiparty Politics and Ghost Towns
960.label: Event
960.description: Villes mortes (ghost town) campaign; opposition leader John Fru Ndi; contested elections; oil revenues sustain patronage networks.
